paragraphs.text: Yoma 35b: The Sages taught: ‘A poor person, a rich person, and a wicked person come to judgment. The poor person is asked: “Why did you not study Torah?” If he answers, “I was poor and occupied with earning a living,” he is told: “Were you poorer than Hillel?” ... The rich person is asked: “Why did you not study Torah?” If he answers, “I was wealthy and occupied with my property,” he is told: “Were you richer than Rabbi Elazar?” ... The wicked person is asked: “Why did you not study Torah?” If he answers, “I was handsome and preoccupied by my inclination,” he is told: “Were you more handsome than Joseph?” ... Thus Hillel condemns the poor, Rabbi Elazar ben Charsom condemns the rich, and Joseph condemns the wicked.’ See Divrei Sofrim 28, pp. 237–240 in our edition.

paragraphs.text: Nazir 23a: ‘Consider Lot and his two daughters. They intended a mitzvah—“The righteous walk in them”; he intended a transgression—“Sinners stumble in them.” Perhaps he too intended a mitzvah? Rabbi Yochanan said: This entire verse alludes to transgression. “Lot lifted”—“His master’s wife lifted”; “his eyes”—“She is pleasing in my eyes”; “he saw”—“Shechem son of Chamor saw her”; “all the plain of the Jordan”—“For a prostitute, as little as a loaf of bread”; “for it was all watered”—“I shall follow my lovers, who give me my bread and water, my wool and flax, my oil and drink.”’

paragraphs.text: Shaar Maamarei Razal, Midrashim 2:13, in the discourse on Abraham’s strides: ‘Although Leah was rectified and the impurity of the first Eve was removed from her, so that she remained holy and wholly righteous, nevertheless, because of the strength of the dross that had clung to her, Dinah emerged from her. Dinah is harsh judgment, and was therefore named after judgment. She too was holy, but some hold of impurity still remained, for she had not been completely refined.… Afterward Shimon married her.… Dinah’s root is in the powers of severity, harsh judgment, and therefore Shimon took her. Since she had not yet been purified … Shaul, the son of the Canaanite woman, was born from her, as the Sages said: the son of one who had relations with a Canaanite. He himself was Shelumiel ben Tzurishaddai, and he himself was Zimri ben Salu, as the Sages said in Sanhedrin. By the power of that impurity he attached himself to Kozbi. Kozbi, too, was the residue of the impurity associated with Dinah, the mother of Shaul; she was his destined partner, except that he consumed the fruit before it was ripe, for she was not yet fitting.’

paragraphs.text: Nazir 23b: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: ‘How do we know that God withholds not even the reward for refined speech? Concerning the elder daughter, who called her son Moab, God said: “Do not distress Moab or provoke them to war.” War is prohibited, but distressing them is permitted. Concerning the younger daughter, who called her son Ben Ammi, He said: “Do not distress or provoke them”—even distressing them is entirely prohibited.’ Rabbi Chiya bar Avin said in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah’s name: ‘A person should always hasten to perform a mitzvah. Because the elder daughter preceded the younger by one night, she merited preceding her by four generations in Israel’s royal line.’

paragraphs.text: Targum Yonassan to Bereishis 50:13: ‘His sons carried him to the land of Canaan. The matter was heard by the wicked Esau, who came from Mount Geval with many legions to Hebron and would not allow Joseph to bury his father in the Cave of Machpelah. Immediately Naphtali went, ran down to Egypt, and returned that same day, bringing the deed that Esau had written for his brother Jacob concerning his portion in the Cave of Machpelah. Immediately a signal was given to Chushim the son of Dan, who took a sword and cut off the head of the wicked Esau. Esau’s head rolled into the cave and came to rest in the bosom of his father Isaac. Esau’s sons buried his body in the field of Machpelah. Afterward Jacob’s sons buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, the field that Abraham had bought as a burial possession from Ephron the Hittite, opposite Mamre.’

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 2a, Mishnah: ‘For three days before idolaters’ festivals, it is forbidden to transact business with them, lend or borrow articles, lend or borrow money, repay them, or collect repayment from them. Rabbi Yehudah permits collecting repayment because it causes the debtor distress. The Sages answered: Although distressed now, he rejoices afterward.’ The Gemara states: ‘Rav and Shmuel differ: one teaches eideihem with aleph, the other with ayin,’ etc. ‘Neither wording is mistaken: the aleph spelling is supported by “For the day of their calamity is near”; the ayin spelling by “Let them bring their witnesses and be vindicated.” Why does the first not use the ayin spelling? He holds that calamity is the preferable allusion. Why does the second not use the aleph spelling? He answers: What causes their calamity? The testimony they themselves gave; therefore the allusion to testimony is preferable.’

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Behar 110b, Sulam translation: ‘Rabbi Yehudah began: “Trust in the Lord and do good; dwell in the land and nurture faith.” A person should always be attentive to his Master and attach his heart to the supernal faith, so as to be wholehearted with his Master. When he is wholehearted with his Master, none of the world’s people can harm him. Come and see: “Trust in the Lord and do good.” What is “do good”? We have learned that an awakening below awakens the supernal action. They have already explained “You shall perform them”: as it were, you make them, because your awakening below awakens what is above. Therefore it says “do good.” Good refers to the righteous one, Yesod of Zeir Anpin, as it is written: “Say of the righteous that he is good.” When you act thus, this good is certainly awakened above. Then “dwell in the land and nurture faith”: all is one, for land and faith both refer to Malchus.’ The Zohar’s teaching continues in the next three notes.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Behar 110b, continuation of the Sulam translation: ‘He explains: “Dwell in the land”—the supernal land, Malchus. No one in the world can dwell with her until that good, Yesod of Zeir Anpin, is awakened toward her. Without Yesod, Malchus is filled with harsh judgments. When a person awakens it through good deeds, it is as though he makes it. Then “dwell in the land”: dwell within Malchus, eat her fruit, and delight with her. “Nurture faith”—this is the land, Malchus; faith and land are one, both Malchus, as in “Your faithfulness at night,” since night is Malchus. “Nurture faith” means: direct her in all matters as you wish.’

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Behar 110b, continuation of the Sulam translation: ‘If you do not awaken Yesod toward her, this good, Yesod, withdraws from her. Then do not approach her; do not approach the burning furnace, for without Yesod she is filled with judgments like a furnace. If you approach, be fearful, like one afraid of death, for she is then a blazing fire that burns the world with her flames. Once you awaken this good toward her, dwell within her without fear. Then “You shall decree a matter and it shall be established for you, and light shall shine upon your ways.” Come and see: Those of faith direct Malchus according to their will every day, and she fulfills their decrees. Who are those of faith? Those who awaken Yesod toward her by giving charity without sparing their own resources, knowing that God will give them more, as it is written: “One gives freely, yet increases.” Why? Because Yesod awakens blessings toward him. Let him not say, “If I give this now, what shall I do tomorrow?” Rather, God gives him blessings beyond sufficiency, as has been explained.’

Those who awaken Yesod toward her by giving charity without sparing their own resources, knowing that God will give them more, as it is written: “One gives freely, yet increases.” Why? Because Yesod awakens blessings toward him. Let him not say, “If I give this now, what shall I do tomorrow?” Rather, God gives him blessings beyond sufficiency, as has been explained.’

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 82a: Rav said: ‘Pinchas saw Zimri’s act and remembered the halachah. He said to Moses: “My father’s father’s brother, did you not teach me when descending from Sinai: Zealots may strike one who has intercourse with a gentile woman?”’ Zohar, Acharei Mos 57b, Sulam translation: ‘What connection is there between alien fire and a foreign woman? At first they brought what was remote from holiness near to holiness and impaired it, as it is written: “When they offered alien fire.” Here too Zimri committed the same sin: he brought a foreign woman, remote from holiness, near to holiness. He brought the King’s name—the sign of the holy covenant—near to the distant, foreign woman. Immediately, “Pinchas son of Elazar son of Aaron the priest saw and rose from the congregation.” Here he rectified the earlier distortion. A yod was then placed in his name to unite the letters, the mystery of uniting Zeir Anpin and Malchus. He was promised peace, Yesod, called peace, as it is written: “Therefore say: Behold, I give him My covenant of peace.” My covenant itself—Yesod.’ The Zohar continues below in note 360. The primordial kings: Genesis 36:31, ‘These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before a king reigned over the children of Israel.’ The Zohar explains why they reigned before Israel’s kingship and why they died. See Zohar, Vayishlach 177a; Terumah, Sifra DiTzeniusa 176b; Naso, Idra Rabba 142a.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Bamidbar 120b, Sulam translation: ‘When a person has prayed in this manner, through action and speech, and tied the bond of unification, the upper and lower realms are blessed through him. After completing the Amidah, he must present himself as though departing this world. He has separated from the Tree of Life, Zeir Anpin, the mystery of the Amidah, and gathered his feet toward the tree of death that returned his deposit—his soul—in the morning, as in “He gathered his feet into the bed.” Having confessed his sins and prayed about them, he must now be gathered to that tree of death, fall upon his face, and say: “To You, Lord, I lift my soul.” At first, when I went to sleep, I entrusted You with my soul. Now that I have bound the unification, performed the action and speech properly, and confessed my sins, my soul is certainly surrendered to You. That is, he should accept upon himself the surrender of his life.’

paragraphs.text: Berachos 35b: The Sages taught: ‘What does “You shall gather your grain” teach? Since it says “This book of Torah shall not depart from your mouth,” one might understand that literally. “You shall gather your grain” teaches that you should combine Torah with ordinary worldly activity, according to Rabbi Yishmael.’ Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: ‘If a person plows at plowing time, sows at sowing time, harvests at harvest time, threshes at threshing time, and winnows when the wind blows, what will become of Torah? Rather, when Israel do God’s will, their work is done by others, as it is written: “Strangers shall stand and pasture your flocks,” etc. When they do not do His will, they do their own work, as it is written: “You shall gather your grain.” Moreover, they do others’ work, as it is written: “You shall serve your enemy,” etc.’

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Balak 194b, Sulam translation: ‘When the Queen of Sheba came to Solomon, one of her questions was: “How can a snake formed from a bone and possessing three sorceries be caught?” Immediately, “There was no matter concealed from the king that he did not tell her.” She asked because she needed those snakes, formed from Balaam’s bones, but could not catch one. How did he answer the matters in her heart, as it is written: “She spoke to him of all that was in her heart”? “Solomon told her all her matters”: no one in the world can overcome these snakes except through one secret—boiling semen. Who can do this? When a person emits semen in passionate desire, directing that desire toward the snake, the hot emission is immediately caught in a cloth and the cloth thrown toward the snake. It immediately lowers its head and is caught like a domestic rooster.’

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Shelach Lecha 169a, Sulam translation: ‘The head of the academy said: King Solomon did not know this detail: that voice comprises the spirit, the soul, and the vapor of the bones arising from the formation of the flesh. This vapor is the body’s formation, as in “Your hands fashioned and made me,” and does not depart from the body as the soul does. The voice wanders in the air, while these three separate from one another. When the voice reaches the place it enters, it sits like one dead. Sorcerers and diviners know these places through their sorcery, bend toward the ground, and hear this voice, in which spirit, soul, and the vapor of the bones join. They disclose what was asked. This is “a medium from the earth.” Solomon therefore pursued knowledge of what is produced by this voice, but did not know it.’

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 104b: Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: ‘The Men of the Great Assembly wished to add another person—King Solomon—to those without a share in the World to Come. His father’s image came and prostrated itself before them, but they paid no attention. Fire descended from heaven and scorched their benches, but they paid no attention. A heavenly voice said: “Have you seen a man skilled in his work? He shall stand before kings, not before obscure men.” He built My house before his own; moreover, he built My house in seven years and his own in thirteen. “He shall stand before kings, not before obscure men.” They paid no attention. A heavenly voice said: “Is it for you to repay him, because you reject him? For you must choose, and not I,” etc.’ Rashi explains: ‘Is punishing a person your responsibility, that you reject Solomon and say he has no share in the World to Come? Is the choice of who has a share yours rather than Mine? The matter depends on Me.’ Sanhedrin 99b: ‘God sought to bring even descendants of that wicked man under the wings of the Divine Presence. The ministering angels said: “Master of the universe, will You bring the descendants of one who destroyed Your house and burned Your sanctuary under the wings of the Divine Presence?” Thus it is written: “We sought to heal Babylon, but she was not healed.”’

paragraphs.text: Gittin 57b: ‘Onkelos son of Kalonikos, a son of Titus’s sister, wished to convert. He raised Titus through necromancy and asked: “Who is esteemed in that world?” “Israel.” “Should I attach myself to them?” Titus answered: “Their commandments are numerous and you cannot fulfill them. Go provoke them in that world and become a leader, as it is written: ‘Her oppressors became the head.’ Whoever oppresses Israel becomes a leader.” Onkelos asked: “What is your punishment?” “What I decreed upon myself: each day they gather my ashes, judge me, burn me, and scatter me over the seven seas.” He raised Balaam and asked: “Who is esteemed in that world?” “Israel.” “Should I attach myself to them?” “Do not seek their peace or welfare all the days.” “What is your punishment?” “Boiling semen.” He raised the sinners of Israel—the figure identified here as Yeshu—and asked: “Who is esteemed in that world?” “Israel.” “Should I attach myself to them?” “Seek their welfare, not their harm. Whoever touches them is as though touching the apple of His eye.” “What is your punishment?” “Boiling excrement,” for the Master said: “Anyone who mocks the Sages’ words is judged in boiling excrement.” Come and see the difference between Israel’s sinners and the prophets of the idolatrous nations.’

paragraphs.text: Shabbos 30a: Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: ‘What does “Show me a sign for good, so that those who hate me see and are ashamed” mean? David said before God: “Master of the universe, forgive that sin!” God answered: “You are forgiven.” David asked: “Show me a sign during my life!” God answered: “I shall not make it known during your life, but during the life of your son Solomon.” When Solomon built the Temple and sought to bring the Ark into the Holy of Holies, the gates clung together. He offered twenty-four expressions of prayer and was not answered. He began: “Lift up your heads, gates; be lifted, everlasting doors, that the King of glory may enter.” They rushed to swallow him and asked: “Who is this King of glory?” He answered: “The Lord, mighty and strong.” He repeated: “Lift up your heads, gates; lift up, everlasting doors, that the King of glory may enter. Who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts; He is the King of glory, Selah.” He was not answered. Once he said: “Lord God, do not turn away Your anointed one; remember the kindnesses of David Your servant,” he was answered immediately. At that moment the faces of David’s enemies became black like the bottom of a pot, and all the people and all Israel knew God had forgiven that sin.’

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Beshalach 52b, Sulam translation: Rabbi Shimon said: ‘There is a doe in the land for whose sake God does much. When she cries, God hears her distress and receives her voice. When the world needs mercy for water, she cries out, God hears her voice, and He has mercy upon the world. Thus it is written: “As a deer longs for streams of water.” When she needs to give birth, she is closed on every side. She places her head between her knees, cries, and raises her voice. God has mercy upon her and sends a snake that bites her at her opening, opens and splits that place, and she gives birth immediately.’ Rabbi Shimon said: ‘In this matter, do not question or test the Lord. This is precisely how it is.’ Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Festival of Matzos 8: ‘We shall explain the doe bitten by a snake at her opening, as mentioned in Beshalach. Malchus is the doe beloved by her husband, Zeir Anpin. She united with him on the first night of Pesach and conceived from that union; she gives birth on Pesach’s seventh day. Since she is not yet fully rectified—Zeir Anpin himself is in a state of diminished consciousness, and all the more so she—she is called a doe whose womb is narrow. She has only the five powers of severity, the letters mem, nun, tzadi, peh, and kaf, the mystery of the barley omer offered on Pesach’s second day. Se’arah, “barley,” has the numerical value 575: the two occurrences of these five letters, each totaling 280, become 285 when their five letters are included. Twice 285 is 570, and including five within five gives 575, the value of se’arah. Her womb is therefore narrow, for the female aspect does not yet possess the five kindnesses. She cannot give birth, for the external forces would seize those offspring, the souls issuing from complete union, since this is still a time of diminished consciousness. Therefore the supernal snake bites her opening: Yesod in its diminished state unites with her. This union is termed a bite because diminished consciousness is judgment. Through it her narrow womb opens, the external forces draw off the impurity and judgment, and holiness remains. They touch only the aspect of the snake, not the expanded consciousness; there is no need to elaborate further. This is the mystery of the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, the female’s womb; she gives birth through the snake. Thus the Zohar in Beshalach says: “Why do you cry to Me? The matter depends on Atika.” Since Zeir Anpin is in a diminished state, he is unfit for union unless the supernal level shines upon him with its great power. Zeir Anpin clothes Netzach, Hod, and Yesod of Atika; Atika awakens to illuminate him, enabling him to unite. The other lights of Abba and Imma cannot accomplish this without Atika; therefore the matter depends upon it.’

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 91a: ‘Antoninus told Rabbi: “Body and soul can exempt themselves from judgment. The body says: ‘The soul sinned; since it departed from me, I lie like a silent stone in the grave.’ The soul says: ‘The body sinned; since I departed from it, I fly through the air like a bird.’” Rabbi answered: “I shall give you a parable. A mortal king had a fine orchard with fine early-ripening fruit. He stationed two guards there, one lame and one blind. The lame guard told the blind one: ‘I see fine fruit in the orchard. Carry me, and we shall bring it to eat.’ The lame man rode upon the blind man; they brought the fruit and ate it. Later the owner asked: ‘Where is the fine fruit?’ The lame man answered: ‘Do I have legs to walk?’ The blind man answered: ‘Do I have eyes to see?’ The owner placed the lame man upon the blind man and judged them together. Likewise, God brings the soul, places it in the body, and judges them together.”’

paragraphs.text: Koheles Rabbah 7:1: Rabbi Pinchas said: ‘...When a person is born, everyone rejoices; when he dies, everyone weeps. It should be otherwise. At birth they should not rejoice, for they do not know what circumstances and deeds await him, whether righteous or wicked, good or bad. At death they should rejoice that he departed with a good name and left the world in peace. Two ships sail upon the great sea: one leaves the harbor and one enters. Everyone rejoices over the departing ship, but not over the arriving one. A perceptive man said: “I see the opposite of what should be. Do not rejoice over the departing ship, for you do not know what awaits it, what seas and dangers it will encounter. Rejoice over the ship entering the harbor, for it has arrived safely.” Likewise, when a person dies, all should rejoice and give praise that he departed the world peacefully with a good name. Thus Solomon said: “The day of death is better than the day of birth.”’

paragraphs.text: Niddah: The Sages taught: ‘The people of Alexandria asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananyah twelve questions... Three concerned worldly conduct. “What should a person do to become wise?” He answered: “Spend much time in the academy and little in business.” They said: “Many have done so without success!” Rather, let them seek mercy from the One to whom wisdom belongs,’ etc. What does this teach? That neither effort nor prayer suffices without the other. ‘“What should a person do to become wealthy?” “Engage much in business and deal faithfully.” “Many have done so without success!” Rather, let him seek mercy from the One to whom wealth belongs, as it is written: “The silver is Mine and the gold is Mine.” What does this teach? Neither suffices without the other. “What should a person do to have sons?” “Marry a suitable wife and sanctify himself during intercourse.” “Many have done so without success!” Rather, let him seek mercy from the One to whom children belong, as it is written: “Children are the Lord’s inheritance; the fruit of the womb is a reward.” What does this teach? Neither suffices without the other.’

God said: “Turn around.” Moses sat at the end of eight rows and could not understand what they were saying; his strength failed. When they reached one matter, the students asked: “Rabbi, from where do you know this?” Rabbi Akiva answered: “It is a halachah transmitted to Moses at Sinai.” Moses was reassured. He returned before God and asked: “You have such a man, yet give the Torah through me?” God answered: “Be silent; thus it arose in My thought.” Moses asked: “You have shown me his Torah; show me his reward.” God said: “Turn around.” He saw Rabbi Akiva’s flesh being weighed in the meat market and asked: “Master of the universe, this is Torah and this its reward?” God answered: “Be silent; thus it arose in My thought.”’

paragraphs.text: Yoma 20b: ‘A baraita supports Rav: What did Gevini the herald proclaim? “Priests, arise for your service; Levites, for your platform; Israelites, for your attendance.” His voice was heard three parasangs away... Nevertheless, the High Priest surpassed him, for the Master said: When he said “Please, Lord,” his voice was heard in Jericho. Rabbah bar bar Chanah said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Jerusalem to Jericho is ten parasangs. This is despite the High Priest’s weakness, unlike the herald, and despite his speaking by day while the herald spoke at night. Rabbi Levi said: Why is a person’s voice not heard by day as it is by night? Because the sun’s sphere saws through the firmament like a carpenter sawing cedars... The Sages taught: Three sounds travel from one end of the world to the other: the sound of the sun’s sphere, the tumult of Rome, and the soul departing the body. Some add childbirth.’

paragraphs.text: Eruvin 53a: Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: ‘The people of Judah, who were particular about their language, retained their Torah; the people of Galilee, who were not, did not retain it.’ Does this depend on being particular? Rather, Judah’s people used precise language and employed mnemonics, and retained their Torah; Galilee’s people did neither and did not. Judah’s people learned from one teacher and retained their Torah; Galilee’s people did not learn from one teacher and did not retain it. Ravina said: ‘Judah’s people publicly disclosed their learning and retained it; Galilee’s people did not and did not retain it.’ David disclosed his learning—Rashi: he labored in Torah and issued rulings—while Saul did not. Of David it is written: ‘Those who fear You shall see me and rejoice’; of Saul: ‘Wherever he turned, he condemned’—he did not merit ruling according to the halachah.

paragraphs.text: Sanhedrin 93b: ‘One of the servants said: “I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play, is mighty in valor, a warrior, discerning in speech, handsome, and the Lord is with him,” etc. Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: Doeg spoke this entire verse as malicious speech. “Knows how to play”—knows how to ask questions; “mighty”—knows how to answer; “warrior”—knows how to debate in Torah’s battle; “discerning in speech”—infers one matter from another; “handsome”—shows grounds in halachah; “the Lord is with him”—the halachah follows him everywhere. Of Saul it is written: “Wherever he turned, he condemned”; of David: “Wherever he turned, he succeeded.”’

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Mishpatim 112b, Sulam translation: ‘Every morning Solomon rose early and turned eastward, toward Tiferes and the middle line, and saw what he saw. He then turned southward, toward Chesed and the right line, and saw what he saw. Then he turned northward, toward Gevurah and the left line, and stood there, lowering his eyes and raising his head. At that moment a pillar of fire and a pillar of cloud came, with a great, powerful eagle upon the cloud. Its right wing was upon the pillar of fire, and its body and left wing upon the pillar of cloud. It brought two leaves in its beak. The cloud, fire, and eagle came and bowed before King Solomon. The eagle lowered itself and gave him the leaves. Solomon took and smelled them, recognized their signs, and said: “This belongs to the Fallen One, and this to the Open-Eyed One.” When there were two leaves, he knew both wished to disclose matters to him,’ etc. The Zohar’s account continues below in note 522.

paragraphs.text: Avodah Zarah 44b, Mishnah: ‘Proclus son of Philosophos asked Rabban Gamliel in Acre, while he bathed in Aphrodite’s bathhouse: “Your Torah says, ‘Let nothing of the banned property cling to your hand.’ Why do you bathe here?” He answered: “One does not answer in a bathhouse.” After leaving, he said: “I did not enter her domain; she entered mine. They do not say, ‘Let us make a bathhouse to adorn Aphrodite,’ but ‘Let us make Aphrodite to adorn the bathhouse.’ Moreover, even for much money you would not enter your idol’s sanctuary naked, after a seminal emission, or urinate before it. This image stands over the drain, and everyone urinates before it. paragraphs.text: Alfa Beisa DeRabbi Akiva 6: ‘Every name in the divine chariot has a seal and an appellation. God sits upon a throne of fire, surrounded by explicit divine names like pillars of fire, each in ranks of fire, each with the appearance of fire. With them are many hosts of fiery princes and mighty formations of fiery troops. When a person employs them, every firmament fills with fire, and they descend to burn the world. Reaching the earth, they see the edges of heaven bound to the earth’s edges, and the earth’s edges bound to heaven’s, sealed with the ring “I shall be what I shall be.” They immediately cease their anger and act mercifully toward the whole world and the person employing them. Had God not sealed the world’s four directions with His seal, the world would immediately fill with fire when a person employed them.’

paragraphs.text: Gittin 68b, after describing how Solomon imprisoned Ashmedai, king of the demons: ‘One day Solomon was alone with him and asked: “It is written, ‘Like the heights of the re’em are his powers.’ We explain ‘heights’ as the ministering angels and ‘re’em’ as the demons. What makes you greater than us?” Ashmedai answered: “Remove my chain and give me your ring, and I will show you.” Solomon did so. Ashmedai swallowed it, placed one wing in heaven and one on earth, and cast him four hundred parasangs away. Solomon then said: “What advantage has a person in all his labor under the sun?” “This was my portion from all my labor”—what was “this”? Rav and Shmuel disagree: one says his staff, the other his drinking vessel. He went from door to door, declaring: “I, Koheles, was king over Israel in Jerusalem.” When he reached the Sanhedrin, the Sages said: “A madman does not remain fixed on one claim; what is this?” They asked Benayahu whether the king summoned him; he said no. They asked the queens whether the king visited them; they said yes. They told them to inspect his feet. They replied that he came in slippers, demanded relations during their menstrual periods, and even demanded relations with his mother Bathsheba. They brought Solomon and gave him a ring and chain engraved with the divine name. When he entered, Ashmedai saw him and fled, yet Solomon remained afraid of him. Thus it is written: “Behold, Solomon’s bed, surrounded by sixty mighty men of Israel, all holding swords, trained in war, each with his sword upon his thigh because of fear at night.” Rav and Shmuel disagree: one says he was king and then a commoner; the other, king, commoner, and king again.’

paragraphs.text: Bava Metzia 84a: ‘One day Rabbi Yochanan was bathing in the Jordan. Reish Lakish saw him and leapt in after him. Rabbi Yochanan said: “Your strength should be for Torah!” Reish Lakish answered: “Your beauty should be for women!” Rabbi Yochanan said: “If you repent, I shall give you my sister, who is more beautiful than I.” He accepted. When he tried to leap back to fetch his clothes, he could not. Rabbi Yochanan taught him Scripture and Mishnah and made him a great scholar. One day they disputed in the study hall: A sword, knife, dagger, spear, hand sickle, and harvesting sickle become susceptible to impurity when their manufacture is complete. When is that? Rabbi Yochanan said: When tempered in the furnace; Reish Lakish said: When polished in water. Rabbi Yochanan said: “A robber knows his robbery!” Reish Lakish answered: “How did you benefit me? There they called me master, and here they call me master.” Rabbi Yochanan replied: “I benefited you by bringing you beneath the wings of the Divine Presence.” Rabbi Yochanan became distressed and Reish Lakish fell ill,’ etc. ‘Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish died, and Rabbi Yochanan grieved greatly,’ until his mind became deranged. ‘The Sages sought mercy for him, and he died.’ Rashi explains ‘They called me master’: ‘I was the robbers’ teacher and chief.’ Tosafos explain that he was originally a Torah scholar called Rabbi, then cast off the yoke and became unlearned. On 83b, Rabbi Elazar ben Shimon is described arresting thieves and handing them over for execution, saying: ‘I am removing thorns from the vineyard.’

paragraphs.text: Megillah 6a: Rabbi Yitzchak said: ‘Leshem is Paneas. “Ekron shall be uprooted” refers to Caesarea, daughter of Edom, which was a metropolis of kings.’ Some say that kings were raised there; others say that kings were appointed from there. ‘Caesarea and Jerusalem: if someone tells you that both are destroyed, do not believe it; that both are inhabited, do not believe it. If Caesarea is destroyed and Jerusalem inhabited, or Jerusalem destroyed and Caesarea inhabited, believe it. It is written: “I shall be filled, now that she is laid waste.” If this one is full, the other is destroyed; if that one is full, this one is destroyed.’ Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak derived it from: ‘One nation shall prevail over the other.’ Ekron was in Dan’s inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Vayechi 250a, Sulam translation: ‘Solomon erred in this, for he saw that the moon had drawn near to the sun: the right side of Zeir Anpin embraces her with lovingkindness, and the left side of Zeir Anpin is beneath her head, with the illumination of wisdom. The left became her head. Since the right and left had drawn close to one another, and the wisdom of the left had already been clothed in the right, he said: “They have already drawn close together; what further purpose does the right serve here?” For the right, which is lovingkindness, serves only to bring Zeir Anpin and the female aspect together, so that the female aspect’s wisdom may be clothed in Zeir Anpin’s lovingkindness. Since they have already drawn close to one another, why is the right, lovingkindness, still needed? Immediately, “silver was accounted as nothing in Solomon’s days,” for he rejected silver, which is the right.’

paragraphs.text: ‘What is this voice of a woman to which the snake’s voice can attach itself, like a male dog to a female dog? He answers: Come and see: among all the voices of women in the world, the snake’s voice can cling to and join itself to those of only two women. One is a woman who does not properly observe the impurity of menstruation and her days of purification, or who immerses one day too early. The other is a woman who delays her time for marital intimacy in order to cause her husband distress, unless her husband is not particular about it and pays it no attention.’
